items.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995
items.q: I worked with a saxophone player by the name of Tooty Boyd who has passed on since then, but we used to drive down to Portland for a job

ctx.x: And in Seattle, when you were still in the service, what was going on there?

Well I had a job then, yeah, I had a steady job. I worked with a saxophone player by the name of Tooty Boyd who has passed on since then, but we used to drive down to Portland for a job and I had some jobs in Seattle on Jackson Street, which was a hot street in Seattle at that time. So I made more outside of the Army than I made in the Army.
Yeah? Today we think of a gig as usually nine to one, ten to two, sometimes less than that. What was a typical night like back then?
